statement: Let n = len(nums). The function returns a result r and: if there exists k with 0 ≤ k < n and nums[k] = target, then len(r) = 2, 0 ≤ r[0] < n, 0 ≤ r[1] < n, r[0] ≤ r[1], nums[r[0]] = target, nums[r[1]] = target, for every i with 0 ≤ i < r[0] we have nums[i] ≠ target, and for every i with r[1] < i < n we have nums[i] ≠ target; otherwise, i.e. if no such k exists, len(r) = 2, r[0] = -1, and r[1] = -1.
preconditions: 0 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 100000; nums is non-decreasing, i.e. for every i and j with 0 ≤ i ≤ j < len(nums), nums[i] ≤ nums[j]; and every element of nums and target lies in [-1000000000, 1000000000].
